title: Rigveda 4.8: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.8: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.8 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 264v-265r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.8.1-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 5, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 264v
translation.original_text:
1dū̱taṁ vo̍ vi̱śvave̍dasaṁ havya̱vāha̱m ama̍rtyam | yaji̍ṣṭham ṛñjase gi̱rā ||
2sa hi vedā̱ vasu̍dhitim ma̱hām̐ ā̱rodha̍naṁ di̱vaḥ | sa de̱vām̐ eha va̍kṣati ||
3sa ve̍da de̱va ā̱nama̍ṁ de̱vām̐ ṛ̍tāya̱te dame̍ | dāti̍ pri̱yāṇi̍ ci̱d vasu̍ ||
4sa hotā̱ sed u̍ dū̱tya̍ṁ ciki̱tvām̐ a̱ntar ī̍yate | vi̱dvām̐ ā̱rodha̍naṁ di̱vaḥ ||
translation.text:
1YOUR envoy who possesses all, Immortal, bearer of your gifts, Best worshipper, I woo with song.
2He, Mighty, knows the gift of wealth, he knows the deep recess of heaven: He shall bring hitherward the Gods.
3He knows, a God himself, to guide Gods to the righteous in his home: He gives e'en treasures that we love.
4He is the Herald: well-informed, he doth his errand to and fro, Knowing the deep recess of heaven.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 264v (numbered 73v by the scribe) (OPenn image 265, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.7.10 ‹asya vātaḥ anu-vāti śociḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 265r (numbered 74r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.8.5 ‹-puṣyantaḥ indhate›. Verses 4.8.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1dūtam | vaḥ | viśva-vedasam | havya-vāham | amartyam | yajiṣṭham | ṛñjase | girā
2saḥ | hi | veda | vasu-dhitim | mahān | ārodhanam | divaḥ | saḥ | devān | ā | iha | vakṣati
3saḥ | veda | devaḥ | ānamam | devān | ṛta-yate | dame | dāti | priyāṇi | cit | vasu
4saḥ | hotā | saḥ | it | oṃ iti | dūtyam | cikitvān | antaḥ | īyate | vidvān | ārodhanam | divaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 4.8.5-8 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 5, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 265r
translation.original_text:
5te syā̍ma̱ ye a̱gnaye̍ dadā̱śur ha̱vyadā̍tibhiḥ | ya ī̱m puṣya̍nta indha̱te ||
6te rā̱yā te su̱vīryai̍ḥ sasa̱vāṁso̱ vi śṛ̍ṇvire | ye a̱gnā da̍dhi̱re duva̍ḥ ||
7a̱sme rāyo̍ di̱ve-di̍ve̱ saṁ ca̍rantu puru̱spṛha̍ḥ | a̱sme vājā̍sa īratām ||
8sa vipra̍ś carṣaṇī̱nāṁ śava̍sā̱ mānu̍ṣāṇām | ati̍ kṣi̱preva̍ vidhyati ||
translation.text:
5May we be they who gratify Agni with sacrificial gifts, Whocherish and enkindle him.
6Illustrious for wealth are they, and hero deeds, victorious, Who have served Agni reverently.
7So unto us, day after day, may riches craved by many come, And power and might spring up for us.
8That holy Singer in his strength shoots forth his arrows swifter than The swift shafts of the tribes of men.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 265r (numbered 74r by the scribe) (OPenn image 265, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.8.5 ‹-puṣyantaḥ indhate›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 265v (numbered 74v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.9.5 ‹-janānām havyā ca mānuṣāṇām›. Verses 4.8.5-8 end on this page; 4.8.5 begins on fol. 264v (numbered 73v by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
5te | syāma | ye | agnaye | dadāśuḥ | havya-dātibhiḥ | ye | īm | puṣyantaḥ | indhate
6te | rāyā | te | su-vīryaiḥ | sasa-vāṃsaḥ | vi | śṛṇvire | ye | agnā | dadhire | duvaḥ
7asme iti | rāyaḥ | dive--dive | sam | carantu | puru-spṛhaḥ | asme iti | vājāsaḥ | īratām
